newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - FEB 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - FEB 12.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - At the reque st of all three coalition parties, parliament began discussions yesterday on the Czech-German Declaration, which was signed on January 21 this year in Prague. The pressure from the coalition quickly to address the issue of the declaration ended the possibility of creating an accompanying document, about which Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and Chairman of parliament Milos Zeman met the previous day.
- The four percent unemployment rate recorded at the end of January this year is so far the highest in the history of the Czech Republic.

- Retail within the Czech Republic will most probably have enormous competition this year. Many foreign retail companies have big plans, including Penny Market and Makro, for the expanding market, as well as domestic corporation Interkontakt. PRAVO - The chairman of the board of directors and the executive director of Vitkovice a.s., Vaclav Pastrnak, announced in Ostrava yesterday, that current reports show the company had losses in 1996 of 765 million crowns.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Transport Minister Martin Riman suddenly removed his deputy, Dalibor Zeleny, yesterday from his position because he was unable to resolve discrepancies between Czech Railways, its administrative council, the union and the Transport Ministry. The general director of Czech Railways was expected to be the first official removed from his position.

LIDOVE NOVINY - The executive director of Poldi Steel and agent for Bohemia Art, Marco Stehlik, was released from prison yesterday on bail of three million crowns. Stehlik expressed his intention to obtain debts which are owed to Poldi and pay employees their wages.
